source_read: PMC HTML, PMC4918768 (accepted author manuscript): abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, Table 1 (HTML), Discussion, acknowledgments and disclosure read in full; Figures 1 and 2 read on the rendered images (Figures 3-4 legends only).

claims.note: This source supplies the plasma and early-peak parts: plasma rose for 4 h then declined, while cardiovascular and subjective peaks came within about 15 min. Figure 1 shows the lower doses plateauing from about 90-180 min to 240 min, so 'peaked about 3-4 h' is fair; it also shows nuance in 'within about 15 minutes': after 25 mg/70 kg heart rate peaked at 30 min and diastolic pressure stayed near its peak to 90 min, and blood pressure after 50 mg remained elevated at 240 min. The 24-h heart-rate statement is not from this study: cardiovascular measures stopped at 240 min (only plasma was sampled at 6, 12 and 24 h), and this study had three, not four, active conditions.

anchors.locator: Results > Plasma Methamphetamine Levels; Figure 1 (upper left, rendered image); Methods > Experimental Day
anchors.extracted: Plasma methamphetamine rose dose-dependently (F(3,330)=121.57, p<0.0001) and peaked 4 h after dosing, declining thereafter. Figure 1: after 50 mg/70 kg about 113 ng/ml at 240 min, about 100 at 6 h, about 71 at 12 h, about 35 at 24 h; 25 mg about 55 at 180-240 min; 12 mg about 24 from 90 to 240 min. Sampling at 5-240 min, then 6, 12 and 24 h.

anchors.locator: Results > Cardiovascular Effects and Subjective Effects; Figures 1-2 (rendered); Abstract
anchors.extracted: Heart rate, systolic and diastolic pressure peaked within 15 min of insufflation; subjective peaks at 15 min (abstract: about 5-15 min), while plasma was still rising. Figure 1: 50 mg heart rate about 96 bpm at 15 min vs about 78 after placebo; 25 mg heart rate peaks at 30 min. Cardiovascular monitoring ended at 240 min; the Discussion gives the single-dose cardiovascular duration as more than 240 min.

claims.overstatement: Minor: 'at the largest dose also raised ratings of jitteriness, sweating and a racing heart' is accurate for 50 mg, but jitteriness was also significantly raised at 12 mg (not at 25 mg) and 'heart beating faster' at 25 mg; only sweating was confined to the largest dose. The study population is 11 people (2 women) with DSM-IV methamphetamine abuse (2) or dependence (9), all primarily intranasal users, and each had received the largest dose once before the study, which should be kept in the claim's population wording ('adults who used methamphetamine regularly').
claims.note: Every number in the magnitude field matches Table 1: good drug effect 4.36 / 46.46 / 58.27 / 78.64; high 7.00 / 42.18 / 55.82 / 73.18; at 50 mg vs placebo jittery 24.82 vs 7.36, sweating 25.09 vs 2.09, heart beating faster 43.18 vs 11.27. Table 1 values are means of individual peak ratings (the plotted group means peak lower, about 45 and 75 for 25 and 50 mg). Dose-relatedness: good drug effect and high at 50 mg differed from both lower doses; heart rate at 25 and 50 mg exceeded 12 mg; blood pressure at 50 mg exceeded both lower doses. Cardiovascular magnitudes are in Figure 1 only.

anchors.extracted: 11 non-treatment-seeking adults (9 men, 2 women; mean age 30.7), DSM-IV methamphetamine abuse (2) or dependence (9), primarily intranasal use 3.6 days/week for 6.1 years on average; in-patient, within-participant, double-blind, placebo (lactose) and 12, 25, 50 mg/70 kg single intranasal doses at least 72 h apart; the first two participants received ascending order, the rest counterbalanced; every participant received the 50 mg/70 kg dose once before the study.

Heart rate F(3,240)=13.05, systolic F(3,240)=43.37, diastolic F(3,240)=33.52, all p<0.0001; active doses differed from placebo (p<0.04); heart rate after 25 and 50 mg exceeded 12 mg; blood pressure after 50 mg exceeded the other doses. Figure 1 (approximate): systolic about 144 mmHg at 5 min after 50 mg vs about 113 after placebo.

Peak VAS (0-100, mean, SEM) placebo / 12 / 25 / 50 mg: good drug effect 4.36 / 46.46 / 58.27 / 78.64 (all active vs placebo; 50 vs 12 and 25); high 7.00 / 42.18 / 55.82 / 73.18; stimulated 14.46 / 43.55 / 56.36 / 78.64; jittery 7.36 / 22.73* / 14.73 / 24.82*; sweating 2.09 / 10.73 / 17.91 / 25.09*; heart beating faster 11.27 / 27.18 / 31.82* / 43.18*; nose burning raised at 25 and 50 mg; hunger, sleepy and tired lowered at all doses.
Good drug effect F(3,180)=14.93 and stimulated F(3,180)=11.03, both p<0.001, dose-dependent; peaks at 5-15 min; ratings returning toward baseline by 240 min while plasma was at its highest.

Authors note the single-dose design; citing anecdotal reports that people often take repeated doses over hours to days, they say real-world plasma levels may be much higher; effects of repeated dosing were not tested.

claims.note: Supports the task-level statements. Performance was measured only up to 240 min after dosing in this study, so the magnitude field's 'no residual effects at 24 h' cannot come from it (presumably Kirkpatrick et al., 2012). The review of 16 single-dose studies is another source. The abstract calls 12 and 25 mg the 'intermediate doses'; the claim's 'two smaller of three doses' is the accurate description.

anchors.locator: Results > Psychomotor/Cognitive Performance Effects; Methods > Subjective-Effects and Cognitive/Psychomotor Battery; Discussion para 1
anchors.extracted: After 2 training sessions (3-4 h each) to minimise learning effects, tasks at 15, 60, 120, 180 and 240 min: divided attention task - all doses shortened hit latency and raised maximum tracking speed (p<0.05); DSST - 12 and 25 mg, not 50 mg, increased attempts and correct responses (p<0.03); no other significant effects (repeated acquisition, rapid information processing, immediate and delayed digit recall); no dose produced significant disruption. n=11; no effect sizes; values only in Figure 4.

key_findings.correction: Figure 1 (rendered) is readable: after 50 mg/70 kg plasma about 113 ng/ml at 240 min, about 100 at 6 h (360 min), about 71 at 12 h, about 35 at 24 h; 25 mg about 55 at 180-240 min; 12 mg about 24 from 90 to 240 min.

Figure 1 (rendered, approximate): heart rate after 50 mg about 96 bpm at 15 min vs about 78 after placebo; after 25 mg the heart-rate peak is at 30 min (about 93), not within 15 min; systolic about 144 mmHg at 5 min after 50 mg vs about 113; diastolic about 87 vs 66. 'Within 15 min' holds for 50 mg and is approximate for the lower doses.

reporting_issues.note: Checked: plasma 12 sampling points (30 x 11 = 330), cardiovascular 9 (30 x 8 = 240), VAS 7 (30 x 6 = 180).

Resolvable from the rendered Figure 2: VAS time points are 0, 5, 15, 60, 120, 180 and 240 min, i.e., the second omitted time point is 90 min (when the Drug-Effect Questionnaire was given). Seven time points match df 180. The Methods' 'two exceptions' naming only one remains a minor omission.
Checked: nose burning and craving peak means x10 give integers (26, 105, 237, 280; 790, 718, 700, 713), x11 do not; other items fit n=11.

missed: Figures 1 and 2 are legible on the rendered images, so approximate cardiovascular and plasma magnitudes can be extracted (see key findings 2-3 corrections); the card says they cannot.

Hart 2008 measured cardiovascular effects only to 240 min and performance only to 240 min; the 24-h heart-rate statement in cl_meth_pk_intranasal_timecourse and 'no residual effects at 24 h' in the cl_meth_acute_cognition magnitude must rest on another source (Kirkpatrick et al., 2012), and this study had three active conditions, not four.

Figure 1: after 50 mg the plasma level falls from about 71 ng/ml at 12 h to about 35 at 24 h, an apparent half-life of roughly 12 h (editors' rough reading of a plotted mean), consistent with the 10-11 h figure in cl_meth_pk_halflife; could be added as a supporting anchor there if the editors wish.

Table 1 peak values are means of individual peaks; the plotted group-mean curves peak lower (good drug effect about 45 at 25 mg and about 75 at 50 mg in Figure 2). Worth stating where the claim quotes 'peak good drug effect'.
